source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Glaucoma may have no early symptoms, and a comprehensive dilated eye examination can detect disease before additional irreversible vision loss occurs.","B":"Glaucoma reliably produces severe eye pain before optic-nerve damage, so examination is unnecessary in an asymptomatic high-risk person.","C":"A routine blood test detects glaucoma earlier than an eye examination and is the preferred test for people at increased risk.","D":"Glaucoma develops only after severe central vision loss is present, so examination before visual symptoms has little value."}}
source_row.rationale: NEI states that glaucoma can be asymptomatic early and that people at increased risk are best evaluated with comprehensive dilated eye examinations; early detection and treatment can help prevent further vision loss.
